children: The state is considering acquiring up to 5,000 acres near Wadhavan port for a dedicated chemicals park as India targets a USD 1 trillion sector by 2040

Maharashtra is in the final stage of formulating a dedicated chemicals sector policy and aims to announce it by the first week of November, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Thursday. The state is also exploring the acquisition of 2,500–5,000 acres near the upcoming Wadhavan port in Palghar district to develop a dedicated chemicals park.

Speaking at an industry event organised by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), Fadnavis said the proposed policy would support the sector’s long-term growth. The state government has consulted industry leaders over the past few months to understand their requirements, with inputs expected to be incorporated into the policy.Among those consulted were Reliance Industries Executive Director Nikhil Meswani and UPL Chairman Jai Shroff. Fadnavis expressed confidence that the policy would encourage investors to expand their commitments to Maharashtra’s chemicals industry.

Fadnavis said the need for a dedicated chemicals policy became apparent after the state introduced its industrial policy last year. Maharashtra currently has 3,600 entities operating in the chemicals sector, which accounts for 19 per cent of the sector’s gross value added (GVA) and 17 per cent of chemical exports. The industry employs around 300,000 people in the state, he said.

He also highlighted Maharashtra’s existing port infrastructure, including Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), which he described as the country’s largest container port, as a factor supporting the state’s role in the chemicals industry.

The state plans to develop a dedicated chemicals ecosystem near the greenfield Wadhavan port, which Fadnavis said is expected to be ready in about three years. The proposed land acquisition would support the establishment of a Bhavya Rasayanik Park, in line with the Union government’s announcement of Bhavya Rasayan Parks.
The proposed park is intended to create an industrial hub close to the port, supporting connectivity and the development of the chemicals sector.
India Targets USD 1 Trillion Chemicals Sector

Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilisers J P Nadda, who also addressed the event, said the chemicals sector is currently valued at USD 220 billion, with a target of reaching USD 1 trillion by 2040.Nadda identified improved connectivity, supportive policies and industry leadership as factors that could contribute to the sector’s growth. He also said the government would facilitate environmental clearances for upcoming projects as part of its efforts to support capacity expansion.

The minister urged industry players to increase their focus on research and development (R&D). He added that advanced chemicals and petrochemicals are included in a newly launched Rs 1 lakh crore fund aimed at promoting research and innovation.
